task.title: Size a table and its columns
task.shortdesc: By default a table is as wide as its content needs, up to the width of the page. You can give the table a width, give widths to its columns, and choose between two layouts.

step.cmd: Set the width of the table

info.p: A table with width: auto, the initial value, takes the width that its content wants. If the content is wider than the space it has, the table is as wide as the space and the text in the cells wraps. A table with a width has that width, and it can be a length or a percentage. Margins, borders and padding work as for any box, and margin-left: auto with margin-right: auto centers the table:

step.cmd: Let CSSMedia share the width between the columns

info.p: With the initial layout, table-layout: auto, CSSMedia measures the content of all the cells of a column. A column is never narrower than its longest word or other unbreakable content, and it is as wide as its content when there is room. When the table is wider than the content needs, the extra width goes to the columns without a width of their own, in proportion to the width their content asks for. This layout looks at every row, so it gives the best result for most tables, but it must measure all the cells.

A width on a cell makes its column that wide, or wider if another cell of the column needs more. You can also set the width or the min-width on the table-column element of the column, as Turn elements into a table shows. A column with a width does not take part in sharing the extra width of the table:

step.cmd: Use a fixed layout when you know the widths

info.p: With table-layout: fixed and a table width, CSSMedia does not look at the content to find the widths. A column takes the width of its table-column element, or else of its cell in the first row. The columns without a width share the rest of the width of the table equally. The result does not change with the content, and a long word in a cell that is too narrow does not make the column wider. If the table has no width, or its width is auto, the layout is automatic:
Percentages work for the widths of cells and columns in a fixed layout.

image.alt: Two tables with the same content. In the table with the automatic layout, the middle column is wide, and the first and last columns are narrow. In the table with the fixed layout, the three columns have the same width.

info.p: The height of a row is the height of its tallest cell. A height on a row or on a cell is a minimum: the row is taller if its content needs it. If you give the table a height that is more than its rows need, the extra height goes to the rows.
